results.reader_title: Europe loses competitive ground in clean-tech value chains
results.reader_what: Harvard and Bruegel researchers find modest deterioration in Europe’s clean-technology export competitiveness since 2018.
results.reader_why: Weakening industrial capabilities can increase European exposure to imported components of strategic clean-energy technology.
results.reader_more: Ahuja and colleagues combine the Growth Lab Greenplexity index with Bruegel Clean Tech Tracker investments to identify European industrial capabilities across ten green value chains. Their data show uneven regional strengths and some loss of global position. They favour targeting feasible regional industrial clusters rather than subsidising all technologies everywhere.

deep_analysis.research_question: Europe loses competitive ground in clean-tech value chains
deep_analysis.main_finding: Existing industrial clusters can guide credible European investment to protect manufacturing competitiveness.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Full seventeen-page Harvard Kennedy School author paper, including comparative trade indices, figures, methodology and regional results; original Bruegel Working Paper 28/2026 identity corroborated.
deep_analysis.qualification: Trade competitiveness indices describe relative exports and capabilities, not factory closures or future project success.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Direct evidence on European strategic clean-tech industrial capacity and competitive position relative to China and the US.

results.reader_title: Balancing US LNG supplies with European decarbonisation
results.reader_what: CSIS assesses how US natural gas could replace Russian imports without committing Europe to long-lived fossil dependence.
results.reader_why: The supplier and duration of imported gas contracts determine geopolitical leverage and Europe’s energy-market resilience.
results.reader_more: Larsen compares the EU’s urgent need to diversify from Russian gas after the 2022 invasion with transatlantic LNG infrastructure, methane-emissions and net-zero commitments. He outlines near-term supply options and the risks of new fixed import assets in a declining gas-demand scenario. The piece makes a data-supported policy argument, not a later measured market outcome.

results.reader_title: Urgent EU battery industrialisation creates unequal governance trade-offs
results.reader_what: A Finnish battery-industry case study finds urgency can accelerate projects while narrowing public participation and privileging large actors.
results.reader_why: European battery supply-chain localisation relies on permitting, public acceptance and coordination across EU and local bodies.
results.reader_more: Kotilainen and colleagues investigate multilevel governance of European battery industrial expansion, using Finnish case evidence on rapid project development, decision-making at different levels and local concerns. Their analysis finds urgency can skew influence toward resource-rich firms and jurisdictions while restricting consultation and heightening local opposition.

deep_analysis.research_question: Urgent EU battery industrialisation creates unequal governance trade-offs
deep_analysis.main_finding: Building secure European battery production quickly can undermine legitimacy if local governance and consultation lag.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Full original Resources Policy peer-reviewed manuscript, including author list, methods, case findings and discussion, captured in assignment source material.
deep_analysis.qualification: Qualitative Finnish cases illuminate governance mechanisms but cannot establish effects across every EU battery project.
